html:
The Imbangala were bands of warriors who appeared in what is now Angola in the late 1500s and later founded the kingdom of Kasanje on the Kwango River. The map shows their lands in its 1815 snapshot, when Kasanje was a major trading state.

The early Imbangala lived by war. They took in captured boys and raised them as fighters, and followed strict laws that set them apart from settled people. The English sailor Andrew Battell, who lived among them around 1600, left a famous account. They fought both for and against the Portuguese of Luanda, and Queen Nzinga took up their ways when she allied with them.

Around 1620 one band set up Kasanje. For two centuries it bought captives from Lunda to the east and sold them to the Portuguese for the Atlantic slave trade. Portugal brought Kasanje under its rule around 1910.
